Nuisance Learners

Source: R/learners.R
learners.Rd

Learners estimate the two nuisance functions of soft_lm(): the outcome regression \(m(X) = E[Y \mid X]\) and the score regressions \(r_k(X) = E[p_k \mid X]\). Each learner is an object of class softcats_learner that knows how to fit a regression of a numeric response on a data frame of controls and how to predict from that fit. All learners accept observation weights.

  • lrn_ranger() fits a random forest with ranger. It is the default because valid inference requires the nuisances to be estimated well, and both nuisances are typically non-linear.

  • lrn_lm() fits least squares on the controls, optionally with raw polynomial terms of the numeric controls. It is fast and deterministic, and appropriate when the nuisances are close to polynomial.

  • lrn_glmnet() fits a penalised regression with glmnet on a polynomial expansion of the controls, with the penalty chosen by cross-validation.

  • lrn_custom() wraps any user-supplied pair of fit and predict functions.

Usage

lrn_ranger(
  num.trees = 500L,
  mtry = NULL,
  min.node.size = NULL,
  num.threads = 1L,
  ...
)

lrn_lm(degree = 1L)

lrn_glmnet(alpha = 0, degree = 2L, nfolds = 5L, s = "lambda.min", ...)

lrn_custom(fit, predict, name = "custom")

# S3 method for class 'softcats_learner'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

num.trees

[optional] (integer) Number of trees (default: 500).

mtry

[optional] (integer) Number of controls considered at each split, capped at the number of controls. NULL uses the ranger default (default: NULL).

min.node.size

[optional] (integer) Minimum node size. NULL uses the ranger default (default: NULL).

num.threads

[optional] (integer) Number of threads used by ranger. One thread keeps results reproducible across machines (default: 1).

...

[optional] Further arguments passed to ranger::ranger() or glmnet::cv.glmnet(), except those set by the learner (x, y, the weights, seed and verbose). Use the seed argument of soft_lm() for reproducible forests.

degree

[optional] (integer) Highest power of each numeric control in the design matrix (default: 1 for lrn_lm() and 2 for lrn_glmnet()).

alpha

[optional] (numeric) Elastic-net mixing parameter: 0 is ridge, 1 is lasso (default: 0).

nfolds

[optional] (integer) Number of folds for the internal cross-validation of the penalty (default: 5).

s

[optional] (character or numeric) Value of the penalty used for prediction, as in glmnet::predict.cv.glmnet() (default: "lambda.min").

fit

[mandatory] (function) A function function(x, y, w) that returns a fitted model. x is a data frame of controls, y a numeric vector and w a vector of non-negative weights.

predict

[mandatory] (function) A function function(model, newdata) that returns a numeric vector of predictions.

name

[optional] (character) A short label shown in printed output (default: "custom").

x

[mandatory] (softcats_learner) A learner.

Value

An object of class softcats_learner. The print method returns x invisibly.

Details

The learner can be different for the two nuisances: pass learner = list(m = lrn_ranger(), r = lrn_lm(degree = 2)) to soft_lm().

In lrn_lm() and lrn_glmnet(), factor and character controls enter as treatment-coded dummies. A level that does not occur in a training fold is predicted as the first level.

Examples

# Example: Built-in learners
lrn_lm(degree = 2)
#> <softcats learner: lm (degree 2)>
lrn_ranger(num.trees = 200)
#> <softcats learner: ranger>

# Example: Natural splines in the first control, linear in the others
lrn_spline <- lrn_custom(
  fit = function(x, y, w) {
    stats::lm(y ~ splines::ns(x1, df = 4) + x2 + x3,
              data = cbind(x, y = y), weights = w)
  },
  predict = function(model, newdata) {
    stats::predict(model, newdata = newdata)
  },
  name = "natural splines"
)
lrn_spline
#> <softcats learner: natural splines>
